scope: Quantum information and physics research for cycle two; model-specific theorem candidates and scope audits, not external validation or priority clearance.

overall_verdict.status: broad_bounded_holevo_EB_lift_unknown; scoped quantitative advances and interface rejections
overall_verdict.statement: No proof or qualifying bounded-Holevo counterexample for the general approximate-broadcasting-to-EB-lift was obtained. The exact common-channel operator inequality remains open. Composite-spectrum soft clipping is known to fail on a self-compatible qutrit-product example, while the product of factor comparators still works there. An exact non-line-constant d=5 channel also violates the line-peak cover budget, yet has an explicit EB factor-two comparator. A new internally reconstructed qubit subclass proof and a rank-sensitive fermionic completion sharpening are recorded, alongside scoped metrology/control results and boundaries.
overall_verdict.confidence_boundary: Astra W-Z package claims are source-derived and unreviewed unless explicitly attributed to primary published sources. Child calculations, finite diagnostics, and agreement are internal evidence only; no priority claim is made.

claims.exact_statement: For finite-dimensional state-family sequences with uniformly bounded Holevo information, whether a two-output CPTP broadcaster whose two marginals uniformly approach the input family implies a single family-independent EB channel with uniform trace reconstruction error tending to zero, without a dimension/covering condition, remains UNKNOWN in this investigation.
assumptions: Dimensions and family sizes may grow.
Broadcasting error is marginal trace distance uniformly over the family.
The desired reconstruction is one ordinary CPTP measure-and-prepare channel on the full input algebra for each instance, common to every family member.
Holevo information is uniformly bounded; no covering-net growth condition is supplied.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md#target-interface-and-exact-open-lemma; pinned N93-bounded-holevo-gates and cycle-four source d-48ed31af9b1d38fd.html.
claims.novelty_boundary: This is the unresolved Astra target, not a result. Exact cloner lower bounds, Clifford sandwiches with nonvanishing broadcast error, and unbounded-Holevo ladders do not meet the stated premise.
costs: Channel/broadcaster and state-family representation are supplied.
No cost for acquiring the channel or implementing the unknown common measurement is established.
claims.falsifier: A proof of the stated implication or a sequence satisfying every premise but retaining EB error bounded away from zero resolves this UNKNOWN in the corresponding direction.
claims.next_gate: Prove the all-frame common-measurement operator inequality for arbitrary self-compatible maps, or construct a bounded-Holevo vanishing-broadcast-error counterexample.

claims.exact_statement: For any unital Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint CPTP qubit map Phi that is self-compatible, there exists a unital Pauli-diagonal EB channel Psi such that I-Psi is bounded above by 2(I-Phi) in Hilbert-Schmidt superoperator order. After a unitary conjugation diagonalizing the real symmetric Bloch matrix, set nu_i=max(2 lambda_i-1,0); self-compatibility implies the Bell eigenvalues of the Choi state are at most 3/4, which implies sum_i nu_i<=1, the qubit EB condition. On each Pauli eigenoperator, 1-nu_i<=2(1-lambda_i).
assumptions: Input map is a unital, trace-preserving, completely positive qubit map.
The map is self-adjoint for normalized Hilbert-Schmidt inner product.
The map is self-compatible: it is a marginal of a two-output CPTP extension with identical marginals.
Operator inequality is on the Hermitian Hilbert-Schmidt operator space; identity is included.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_exact_finite_dimensional_subclass_theorem; independent review and priority check outstanding
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/broadcast_lift/REPORT.md and CLAIMS.json (being finalized); FINAL_REPORT.md section on the qubit subclass. Monogamy step: for a maximally entangled projector P on reference-system pair, 2 Tr(rho P) <= ||P_1+P_2|| = 1+1/2 = 3/2, so each Bell overlap <=3/4.
claims.novelty_boundary: A dimension-two restricted operator-comparator theorem is not the general bounded-Holevo lift. Known qubit EB geometry and entanglement monogamy are used; priority is not claimed.
costs: The qubit channel or its Bloch matrix and a compatible extension are supplied.
The proof is existential/algebraic and does not charge implementation or channel tomography.
claims.falsifier: A self-compatible unital HS-self-adjoint qubit CPTP map whose diagonal Bloch eigenvalues violate the derived EB clipping constraint or whose resulting Pauli channel fails the displayed superoperator inequality.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof review; the prime-dimensional line-constant Weyl extension is now recorded as QP-03. Next remove line-constancy or find a counterexample.

claims.exact_statement: For prime d, let Φ be a Weyl-covariant unital CPTP channel with real eigenvalue λ_L on each nonidentity Weyl mode in each maximal-isotropic line L, where the d+1 lines partition nonzero phase space. If Φ has a symmetric two-output CPTP extension with both marginals Φ, set ν_L=(2λ_L−1)_+. Then Σ_L ν_L≤1 and Ψ=(1−Σ_Lν_L)D+Σ_Lν_LΔ_L is entanglement breaking, where D is complete depolarization and Δ_L is dephasing in the MUB corresponding to L. It satisfies I−Ψ≼2(I−Φ) in Hilbert-Schmidt order. Negative real λ_L are allowed; the universal cloner attains equality of the constant.
assumptions: Prime dimension d with the standard generalized-Pauli/Weyl phase space and d+1 maximal-isotropic lines.
The channel is Weyl covariant and has line-constant real eigenvalues on nonidentity Weyl modes.
The channel is unital CPTP and self-compatible with equal two-output marginals.
The Choi two-extension may be symmetrized by averaging output swap.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_exact_higher_dimensional_subclass_theorem; independent review and priority check outstanding
claims.proof_path: proofs/weyl_line_comparator.md; FINAL_REPORT.md section following the qubit comparator; work/agents/quantum_physics/broadcast_lift/REPORT.md and CLAIMS.json. Fourier probabilities are p0=[1+(d−1)S]/d² and pg=[1+dλL−S]/d². k=0 is trivial. For 1≤k<d+1 active lines, CP on a least inactive line m gives S≤1+dm and S_inactive≥(d+1−k)m, hence S_active≤1+(k−1)m≤(k+1)/2. If all active, the extension bound p0≤(d+1)/(2d) gives S≤(d+2)/2. Both imply Σ(2λL−1)+≤1; dephasing mixture realizes those modes and the comparator inequality coordinatewise.
claims.novelty_boundary: A restricted line-constant Weyl channel theorem, not the arbitrary-dimension self-compatible-channel lemma and not the bounded-Holevo state-family result. No priority claim; established generalized-Pauli, MUB, and symmetric-extension facts are used.
costs: Exact channel spectrum and prime-d Weyl/MUB representation are supplied.
The proof is algebraic and existential through specified dephasing channels; implementation cost for arbitrary hardware is not assessed.
claims.falsifier: A line-constant self-compatible Weyl channel violating the Fourier probability formulas, Bell-overlap extension bound, clipping mass bound, or final modewise inequality.
claims.next_gate: Extend beyond line-constant spectra using a fractional isotropic-line/frame cover, or find a compatible Weyl-diagonal channel where spectral clipping fails to be EB.

claims.exact_statement: The c=2 operator-comparator property is closed under convex mixtures and direct sums on the represented tracial block algebra. It is also closed under finite tensor products and commuting compositions when each factor has a nonnegative simultaneous spectrum and an EB clipping comparator μ=(2λ−1)+; the resulting comparator is the tensor product/composition of the EB comparators.
assumptions: For mixtures, all maps have the same input/output algebra and their extensions/comparators are mixed with identical weights.
For direct sums, the comparison is on the direct-sum tracial algebra; a full-matrix embedding must separately control off-block coherences.
For tensor products/compositions, factors commute and are jointly diagonal in a Hilbert-Schmidt basis, λ_i,μ_i∈[0,1], and μ_i≥(2λ_i−1)+.
EB comparators compose/tensor to EB channels.
claims.proof_path: FINAL_REPORT.md section following the prime-dimensional Weyl comparator. Mixture and block sum preserve order linearly. For tensor/composition joint modes: if some λ_i≤1/2 then μ-product clipping is zero and λ-product≤1/2; otherwise x_i=2λ_i−1∈[0,1] and ∏(1+x_i)≤2^(n−1)(1+∏x_i), giving 1−∏μ_i≤2(1−∏λ_i).
claims.novelty_boundary: These are structural closure consequences of the comparator construction, not a general higher-dimensional lift. Signed spectra and arbitrary noncommuting compositions are not covered.
costs: The channel factors, simultaneous eigenbasis, and local comparators are supplied.
No tomography or implementation cost is included.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the scalar product inequality under the stated nonnegative spectral assumptions, or a failure of convex-mixture/direct-sum order preservation under the stated algebra contract.
claims.next_gate: Test whether closure extends to signed or noncommuting factors, and identify if any such example is a failure of the product comparator only or a true failure of existence of a common EB map.

claims.exact_statement: There exist two self-compatible line-constant Weyl-covariant qutrit channels Phi_1 and Phi_2, each a convex mixture of the d=3 universal 1-to-2 cloner marginal D_(5/8) and MUB dephasing channels, such that the product channel is self-compatible but the candidate comparator obtained by clipping its composite Weyl spectrum as mu_g=(2 lambda_g-1)_+ is not completely positive. For the exact rational mixture weights in FINAL_REPORT.md, its inverse-Weyl probability at g=((2,1),(1,0)) equals -71/162000.
assumptions: The four qutrit lines are ordered by slopes 0, 1, 2, then vertical; each dephasing channel is complete dephasing in the associated MUB basis.
D_(5/8) is the qutrit marginal of the standard universal 1-to-2 cloner and is self-compatible.

The two channels use mixture weights Phi_1=(1/4)D_(5/8)+(3/4)(3/100 Delta_0+92/100 Delta_1+4/100 Delta_2+1/100 Delta_infinity) and Phi_2=(39/50)D_(5/8)+(11/50)(33/100 Delta_0+26/100 Delta_1+36/100 Delta_2+5/100 Delta_infinity).
The Weyl eigenvalue convention and inverse Fourier transform are those implemented with exact rational arithmetic in the cited proof script.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/proofs/weyl_clipping_product_counterexample.py; FINAL_REPORT.md paragraph 'A related but different construction'. The script computes both factor spectra and the exact negative inverse-Weyl probability -71/162000.
claims.novelty_boundary: This disproves tensor-stability of the composite-spectrum soft-clipping formula only. It does not refute existence of an EB factor-two comparator; for these factors the tensor product of their EB comparators remains valid by QP-04. No priority claim is made.
costs: The exact channel mixtures and line labels are supplied.
The negative Choi/Weyl probability is an exact algebraic certificate; no channel acquisition or implementation cost is assessed.
claims.falsifier: An error in the rational inverse-Weyl calculation or in the stated self-compatibility of either factor would invalidate this witness.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether non-line-constant Weyl-compatible channels admit a different dimension-independent EB comparator, or find a genuine failure of comparator existence rather than failure of this clipping construction.

claims.exact_statement: For a normalized pure two-form with acquired canonical pair weights w_j>=0 summing to one, independent vacuum loss with particle survival eta<1/2 and discarded environment/flag admits the N100 sector-faithful convex-Gaussian completion with trace-distance error delta <= (1-eta)^2(1-sum_j w_j^2)[u+(1-u)ln(1-u)], u=eta^2/(1-eta)^2. The leading small-eta coefficient is e2=(1-sum_j w_j^2)/2. Rank-one inputs have zero completion error exactly; balanced rank-two inputs have leading coefficient 1/4.
assumptions: Explicit pure two-fermion input and canonical pair amplitudes are supplied/acquired.
Loss is independent and vacuum with block-uniform survival eta<1/2.
The environment and loss record are discarded.
Completion is the sector-faithful convex mixture specified in the N100 construction.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_candidate; Y package and priority not independently reviewed
claims.novelty_boundary: Shape-sensitive sharpening of the source-reported N100 uniform bound; no priority claim. It is not a general fermionic sampling theorem.
costs: Acquire and canonically decompose the two-form, with binomial(m,2) coefficient access.
Charge scalar-root/log precision and any downstream Gaussian sampling separately.

Importing the HNKS channel-estimation theorem yields optimal local QFI Theta(Q) for Q parallel or arbitrary adaptive uses with noiseless ancillas and parameter-independent controls. At omega=0 the span drops to span_H{I,X}, with candidate quadratic coefficient 4c^2, c=(1-exp(-2 gamma tau))/(2 gamma).

The operating frequency is known/calibrated and the claim is pointwise local.
Ancillas, controls, recovery, and measurements are noiseless and uncharged.
The exact-resonance HNKS application uses a differentiable fixed-length Kraus chart through the rank change.

claims.exact_statement: For the exact N81 known-rational pure-Gaussian, uniform-vacuum-loss, specified-binary-herald interface, a uniform constant-TV sampler with polynomial bit runtime on the constructed family would imply PP=BPP (and the quantum analogue PP=BQP). Therefore small loss, exponentially small unconditional vacuum-distance, and bounded conditional energy do not alone provide an efficient conditional sampler; no unconditional sampler lower bound or inverse-success runtime lower bound follows.
assumptions: N81's pure Gaussian construction, loss and herald interface, and reduction error budgets are accepted as stated.
Sampler guarantee is uniform, polynomial in description bits, and TV at most 0.01 on all constructed instances.
claims.status: restricted_source_reduction_candidate; correctness and priority not independently reviewed; no class separation
claims.novelty_boundary: A collapse implication under a specified source-reported reduction, not proof of hardness unless standard complexity classes separate and not a bound proportional to inverse herald probability.
costs: Description-bit complexity, rational precision, herald photon number, filter parameter, and conditional success probability must be separated.
Physical sampler success remains affected by the rare event even when the ideal conditional sampler is efficient.
claims.falsifier: An error-budget or postselection flaw in N81/N82 preventing the stated PP reduction, or a sampler outside the theorem's exact uniform interface used as if it were covered.
claims.next_gate: Independent proof audit of N81/N82 and separately audit N42's bit-complexity composition with the claimed perfect-matching FPRAS.

claims.exact_statement: For the exact finite-N critical Gibbs state rho_N,0 proportional to exp(2J^2/N), every closed-system unitary generated by any time-dependent Hamiltonian commuting with all site permutations leaves rho_N,0 unchanged. For a b-tilted target, trace distance from every such output is at least eta_N(b)/2 where eta_N(b)=Tr[sgn(J_z)rho_N,b]; a nonzero asymptotic floor is conditional on the unreviewed N20 quartic-vector limit.
assumptions: N spin-1/2 sites and J=sum_i sigma_i/2.
Input is exactly rho_N,0 and H(t) commutes with every site permutation at every time.
Evolution is closed-system unitary, without baths, measurement-conditioned branches, reset, or symmetry breaking.
The asymptotic claim assumes the N20 sign-statistic convergence and no mass on J_z=0 in the scaled limit.
claims.status: exact_finite_N_internal_reconstruction; asymptotic extension conditional on source-derived N20 limit
claims.novelty_boundary: Schur-Weyl and Casimir invariance are standard; this model-specific implication is not priority-cleared. It is not a general control no-go when symmetry can be broken or a bath is used.
costs: Input Gibbs preparation and collective sign measurement are supplied.
Control duration, peak field, controller hardware, bath work, and target preparation are unmodeled.
claims.falsifier: A closed unitary commuting with all permutations that changes the exact input state, or an error in the finite-N commuting-observable argument.
claims.next_gate: Reconstruct the N20 finite-N to quartic sign limit and analyze a specified dissipative or symmetry-breaking protocol with work, time, and success costs.

claims.exact_statement: For a density operator rho and a fixed finite sequence of projectors P_1,...,P_m applied sequentially to one global state using Lüders updates, let epsilon_i=Tr((I-P_i)rho) be the rejection probability on the untouched input. Then the all-pass probability is at least 1-4 sum_i epsilon_i, without requiring the projectors to commute.
assumptions: Tests are fixed projective measurements.
Each update is the Lüders instrument.
Errors are evaluated on the same untouched global input.
claims.novelty_boundary: Gao's sequential quantum union bound; does not imply multiplicative repetition or cover arbitrary instruments/adaptive protocols absent history-wise conditions.
costs: m projective measurements on the same shared register; physical measurement time and back-action beyond the ideal instrument are not modeled.
claims.falsifier: A state and fixed Lüders-projector sequence violating the inequality.
claims.next_gate: Use a verifier-specific theorem or establish history-wise conditional pass bounds for any adaptive application.

claims.exact_statement: A count of classical outcome bits does not, without a specified measurement implementation and reset protocol, imply a universal positive work or heat cost for writing a measurement archive; reversible measurement with a supplied pure pointer can defer dissipation to erasure/reset.
assumptions: Ideal thermodynamic operation model with a pure initialized pointer and reversible write.
This does not model a particular laboratory detector, finite-time control, or noisy memory.
claims.status: established_primary_literature_boundary; branch-specific archive capacity corollary is conditional on an unreviewed 2026 preprint
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard information-thermodynamic scope correction, not a new theorem. It does not price acquisition, detector hardware, refresh, or reset unless those interfaces are stated.
costs: Initial pointer purity and eventual erasure/reset conditions must be specified.
Memory Hamiltonian, bath temperature, side information, and retention noise affect physical cost.
claims.falsifier: A theorem under the same ideal reversible-write contract requiring strictly positive work for every write independent of reset or discarded information.
claims.next_gate: Specify a physical detector and memory architecture before making an engineering work/heat claim.

claims.exact_statement: There exists an explicit unital CPTP, Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint, Weyl-covariant self-compatible channel Phi on M_5 whose line-peak budget B=sum_L max_{x in L\{0}}(2 lambda_x-1)_+ equals (6294997+953616 sqrt(5))/6303442>1. The same channel nevertheless admits a single Weyl-covariant entanglement-breaking channel Psi satisfying I-Psi<=2(I-Phi) in Hilbert-Schmidt superoperator order.
assumptions: Phase-space labels are m=(a,b) in Z_5^2 and S((a,b),(u,v))=av-bu.
The exact compatibility witness is q_m=v_m^2/N and X=vv^T/N over Q(sqrt(5)), with v and N as specified in broadcast_lift/D5_AUDIT.md.
The finite Weyl compatibility-kernel criterion of Haapasalo, Corollary 2 Eq. (22), is used to infer self-compatibility.

For the EB comparator, decimal coordinates and positive weights in d5_eb_comparator.json are interpreted as exact decimal rationals; kets and weights are normalized exactly, and the comparator is the rational-weighted mixture of their Weyl-twirled product Choi states.
claims.proof_path: work/agents/quantum_physics/broadcast_lift/D5_AUDIT.md; broadcast_lift/D5_AUDIT_CLAIMS.json; broadcast_lift/scripts/d5_exact_repair_audit.py verifies the exact Q(sqrt(5)) Fourier fixed-vector identities and line budget; broadcast_lift/scripts/d5_rational_interval_comparator.py proves all 24 comparator gaps exceed explicit positive rational thresholds using exact Fraction interval arithmetic and radical endpoints verified by integer squaring.
claims.novelty_boundary: This refutes only the peak-per-projective-line budget extension to arbitrary Weyl spectra. The example itself has a factor-two EB comparator and does not prove or refute the arbitrary-channel comparator lemma or the bounded-Holevo family lift. No priority claim is made.
costs: The channel is specified by 25 algebraic Weyl probabilities and a rank-one 25-by-25 compatibility kernel.
The comparator uses six five-component kets and six positive exact-rational weights; the interval checker verifies 24 scalar mode inequalities.
No acquisition, hardware implementation, or asymptotic cost is assessed.
claims.falsifier: A failure of the exact Fourier fixed-vector equations or compatibility-kernel criterion, a nonpositive certified interval for any of the 24 order gaps, or an error in the stated exact line-budget expression would invalidate this scoped claim.
claims.next_gate: Find a self-compatible Weyl channel for which every EB comparator violates factor-two Hilbert-Schmidt order, or prove a dimension-free comparator theorem beyond line-constant spectra; separately bridge approximate broadcasting to one common EB channel for bounded-Holevo families.
